provenance.usage_policy: known completed logical calls; unresolved provider attempt reservations remain in the cumulative gateway ledger
provenance.sampling_policy: identical prompts with provider defaults, no assumed diversity

dataset.name: Texa Research Benchmark v3 candidate
dataset.split_policy: 300 answerable singles: 100 dev, 200 test. Test strata are 40 basic, 100 compositional, 60 semantic; dev 20/50/30. Each stratum is evenly allocated across Cosmetics Shop and Olist. Query families are labeled by phenomenon, not split prefix; template overlap is intentional and the split is not claimed to be family-disjoint. The three fixture worlds expose controlled grain/coverage changes, and every gold result is authored for each world.

source_capability_notes.cosmetics_shop: challenge-only synthetic events include sessions, views, device and campaign scalar paths.
source_capability_notes.olist_marketplace: challenge-only order item/payment/approval events; no synthetic sessions or viewers. Nested device/campaign fields are declared fixture extensions, not claims about the production source.

dataset.metric_semantics: Olist users are distinct customers observed in order-lifecycle events, not all website visitors. Olist buyer_conversion_rate is buyers divided by observed event-customers; it must not be described as visitor-to-buyer conversion. Purchase revenue is item-line revenue, excluding payment_made event values.
dataset.provenance: Fixture records reused from challenge_v1; this generator independently authors new query specs/SQL and computes expected results in Python for every controlled world. No Texa compiler or LLM generates the gold.
dataset.limitations: Synthetic controlled worlds do not estimate accuracy on live Cosmetics Shop or Olist data. Test labels are visible to the author and the candidate must be externally reviewed and sealed before confirmatory claims.
